and.name: Model_Federation
and.description: All models stay in their own world and do not directly interfere with the language specification of the others (non- intrusiveness); each world is related to the others through meaningful relations that explicit how and why models are related to each other

and.name: Structural
and.description: The graph’s constituents (the nature of vertices; and how edges are organised as well as what they represent), as well as the whole graph.

and.name: Artefacts
and.description: Vertices correspond to Artefacts, as well as the elements they contain

and.name: Domain
and.description: The Domain(s) the Artefacts are intended to be used in. In [1], a feature model describing CPS Domains is available. We extend it with domains outside of CPS. [1] : https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-819105-7.00008-8

and.name: TechSpace
and.description: The technological space (Tech_Space) as defined by [1] is the working context with its set of associated concepts, tools, and possibilities, in which the Artefacts are defined. In the context of MBSE, it crudely refers to the “format” (eg., the MOF meta- meta-model, RDF, textual grammars, etc.) that the Artefact(s) belong to. [1] : Ivan Ivanov, Jean Bézivin, and Mehmet Aksit. 2002. Technological spaces: An initial appraisal. In 4th International Symposium on Distributed Objects and Applications, DOA 2002.

and.name: Formalism
and.description: The Formalism(s) used to specify the Artefacts. [1] proposes a list of Formalisms commonly used for CPS Engineering that we use as a basis for our description. [1] : https://zenodo.org/record/2533455

and.name: Serialisation
and.description: The Serialisation format(s) used for persisting the Artefacts

and.name: Links
and.description: Edges correspond to Links

and.name: Arity
and.description: Refers to the number of artefacts defining, and participating in a Link

and.name: Granularity
and.description: It refers to the specific ‘level’ of decomposition of the linked Artefacts

and.name: Element
and.description: A link exists at the Element level, meaning that structural prop- erties (or model-elements) of the Artefacts are actually linked.

feature.name: Reference
feature.description: The Link simply References the involved Elements, e.g. to indicate that they may be impacted by a change.

feature.name: Content
feature.description: The Link may gives access to the Element’s Content (i.e. the type, in case of a meta-model; or the value, in case of a model), which may be useful for e.g. to propagate values changes throughout interconnected models

feature.name: Model
feature.description: A Link exists at the Model-level, meaning that its target Artefacts are whole models

and.name: Specification
and.description: The Specification feature describes the way Links are defined. This can be fully manual, by linking individual Artefacts for example, or follow a more complex process in which correspondences are defined Manual-ly at the meta-level and then concrete links are Semi-Automatic-ally generated through a matching process. This case indeed relates to the Decomposable-ity of the Link Semantics.

feature.name: Persistence
feature.description: The Links’ Persistence feature characterises MF contributions where Links are persisted, meaning that it is possible to retrieve the Links independently of a modelling session, or after it has ended

and.name: Semantics
and.description: The Semantics associated with the Links. This feature describes the ‘meaning’ of the Links, i.e. why, and for which purpose, the Artefacts are related by the Links.

feature.name: Decomposable
feature.description: It is possible to define Links at a given Granularity, and (semi-)automatically compute and create Links at another level of Granularity.

feature.name: Meta_model
feature.description: The Semantics of Links are explicitly Meta-modelled: this allows Links’ types and relations to be freely and consistently created.

feature.name: MixedLevel

and.name: Federation
and.description: The structural features of the whole MF graph as a singular entity are captured by the Federation feature

feature.name: Process
feature.description: Creation and manipulation of the MF should follow a predefined workflow

and.name: Reified
and.description: The whole MF is manipulable (Artefacts and Links, together).

feature.name: Explicit
feature.description: There exists another single Artefact that explicitly encodes the entire MF,

feature.name: Implicit
feature.description: Modellers need to retrieve pieces of Artefacts they need, by themselves

and.name: Operational
and.description: The processes and operations that are possible, explicitly or implicitly defined, and how they compare with each other.

and.name: Location
and.description: The Location feature describes where the operations take place: they can be attached to the Links, to the Federation, or be completely External to the MF.

and.name: Operations_Typology
and.description: The Operation feature describes which Operations are executed on the MF. Our classification lists some common Op- erations. Representing, Querying, and Constraining Operations on MFs are used to visually display and retrieve models on and from the MF. Syncing an MF aims at resolving inconsistencies between Arte- facts. V&Ving generically designates operations for validating and verifying properties over the MF. Note that this list of operations is generalised and not exhaustive.

and.name: Trigger
and.description: The Trigger is important as it specifies when an Opera- tions shall be executed. An Operation may be triggered Manual-ly and on-demand, or may triggered Reactive-ly to specific events on some parameters from the concerned Artefacts or the MF itself (typically, modifications in the MF)

and.name: ExecutionMode
and.description: Execution Mode. (a.k.a Exec_Mode) specifies how the Oper- ation works. It may work in an Incremental fashion, meaning that whenever it is executed, only the new changes (typically, Links) are computed and/or updated, as opposed to a full Rebuild where everything is recomputed from scratch at each operation invoca- tion.

and.name: Intentional
and.description: Goals or purposes of creating the MF

feature.name: CrossDomainAnalysis
feature.description: Cross-domain analysis involves examining and integrating concepts, methodologies, or technologies from multiple domains to resolve or optimise cross-functional concerns, such as cyber-security, usability, process metrics optimisation, scenario testing, etc.

feature.name: ModelComposition
feature.description: Model composition is a useful modelling activity. For example, in MBSE, where the aim is to build a model of a system by combining existing sub-system models even when the sub-system models are well-developed within their heterogeneous modelling domain(s) or paradigm(s).

feature.name: Traceability
feature.description: Traceability refers to the ability to track and link various stages of the software or system development life-cycle. It includes various activities, such as requirement assignment and verification, impact analysis, compliance and auditing, and project management.

feature.name: ModelConsistencyChecking_Repair
feature.description: Model consistency checking and repair are essential practices in MBSE. Model consistency checking involves verifying that different models do not contradict each other and adhere to predefined rules and constraints, while model repair focuses on automatically or semi-automatically modifying inconsistent model to restore overall consistency.

feature.name: UnifiedTransformationManagement
feature.description: Unified transformation management refers to all tool chains used in software or system production (code generation, reverse engineering, model-to-model transformations). The persistence of transformations enables fine-tuned, incremental management and production traceability of artefacts in a production pipeline.

feature.name: ArtefactCodesign
feature.description: Artefact co-design corresponds to the co-construction of one or more models and their associated meta-model(s), where the model-to-meta-model conformance relationship is not hard-coded in a tool but meta-modelled itself.

feature.name: ReverseEngineering
feature.description: Conceptual elicitation / reverse engineering activities also involve several models, where the aim is to build a conceptual model from various technical artefacts.
